name: Abram's journey to Canaan
summary: From Ur to Haran with Terah, then on to Canaan at God's call, down to Egypt in a famine, and back to settle at Hebron.

stops.note: Terah's family settles here.
God promises the land to Abram's offspring.
Abram goes down to Egypt during a famine.

name: Jacob flees to Haran
summary: After taking Esau's blessing, Jacob flees north to his uncle Laban, meeting God at Bethel on the way.

stops.note: Jacob's dream of the stairway.

name: Jacob returns to Canaan
summary: Twenty years later Jacob returns with his family, wrestles with God at Peniel, and comes home to Isaac at Hebron.

stops.note: Jacob is renamed Israel.

name: Jacob's family goes to Egypt
summary: During the famine, Jacob and his household of seventy move to Goshen to join Joseph.

stops.note: God tells Jacob not to fear going to Egypt.

name: The Exodus: Rameses to Sinai
summary: Israel leaves Egypt on 15 Nisan, crosses the sea, and reaches Mount Sinai in the third month.

stops.note: The sea crossing. Scripture does not give the exact day.

name: From Sinai to Kadesh
summary: The cloud lifts from the tabernacle and Israel sets out north through the wilderness of Paran.

name: From Kadesh to the Plains of Moab
summary: In the fortieth year Israel leaves Kadesh, goes around Edom, and camps opposite Jericho.

stops.note: Aaron dies.
Listed among the camps after Mount Hor (Numbers 33:42).
Around Edom and Moab on the desert side, across the Arnon, and through Sihon's land (Numbers 21:4–35); the exact route is uncertain.

name: Paul's first missionary journey
summary: From Antioch through Cyprus to the cities of southern Galatia, and back the same way to strengthen the new churches.

stops.note: The church sends out Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13:1–3).
The proconsul Sergius Paulus believes.
John Mark leaves them.
Paul turns to the Gentiles (Acts 13:46).
They report how God opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.

name: Paul's second missionary journey
summary: Overland through the Cilician Gates to the Galatian churches, then across to Europe: Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea, Athens and Corinth, returning by Ephesus.

stops.note: Timothy joins Paul and Silas.
The vision of the man of Macedonia (Acts 16:9).
Taken by sea (Acts 17:14–15).
Eighteen months (Acts 18:11).
He "went up and greeted the church" (Acts 18:22), probably at Jerusalem.

name: Paul's third missionary journey
summary: Overland to Ephesus for more than two years, on through Macedonia to Greece, then back by sea to Jerusalem with a gift for its poor.

stops.note: More than two years (Acts 19:10).
2 Corinthians 2:12–13.
Three months in Greece (Acts 20:3), probably at Corinth, where he writes Romans.
Paul goes on foot.
Sighting Cyprus, they leave it on the left (Acts 21:3).

name: Paul's voyage to Rome
summary: Under guard from Caesarea, north of Cyprus to Myra, along Crete, through a fourteen-day storm to Malta, and on to Rome in the spring.

stops.note: Under the lee of Cyprus (Acts 27:4).
Paul warns against sailing on (Acts 27:9–10).
Fourteen days adrift in the storm.
After three months on Malta (Acts 28:11).

name: Israel deported to Assyria
summary: After Samaria falls, the Assyrians carry the people of Israel north around the desert and settle them in Halah, on the Habor, and in the cities of the Medes.

stops.note: On the Habor, the river of Gozan (2 Kings 17:6).

name: Daniel taken to Babylon
summary: The first captives, Daniel and his friends among them, are taken north and down the Euphrates to Nebuchadnezzar's court.

name: Jehoiachin taken to Babylon
summary: The young king, his household, officials, craftsmen and Ezekiel among ten thousand captives are taken the same road to Babylon.

name: Judah taken to Babylon
summary: After Jerusalem falls, its people are marched north to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah and on down the Euphrates to Babylon.

stops.note: Zedekiah sees his sons killed, and is blinded (2 Kings 25:6–7).

name: The first exiles return
summary: Zerubbabel leads about fifty thousand exiles from Babylon back up the Euphrates and down to Judah.

stops.note: By the seventh month they rebuild the altar (Ezra 3:1–2).

name: Ezra's return
summary: Ezra leads a second group home, a four-month journey trusting God for protection instead of asking the king for soldiers.

name: Nehemiah goes to Jerusalem
summary: With the king's letters and an escort, Nehemiah travels from the Persian court at Susa to Jerusalem.

stops.note: Artaxerxes grants Nehemiah leave in the month of Nisan (Nehemiah 2:1–8).

name: Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem
summary: For the census, Joseph goes up from Nazareth to Bethlehem, the town of David, with Mary.

stops.note: No room in the inn (Luke 2:7).

name: The flight to Egypt
summary: Down the coast road to Egypt, and back after Herod's death to Nazareth in Galilee.

stops.note: "Out of Egypt I called my son" (Matthew 2:15).
Archelaus rules Judea, so Joseph goes to Galilee (Matthew 2:22–23).
